The overhang
This electorate-seat focus connects to a mechanism The Spinoff’s Toby Manhire explored last month: MMP’s overhang rule. If Te Pāti Māori wins more electorates than its party vote share would normally entitle it to, those extra MPs don’t get taken away – they expand parliament beyond 120 seats.

Political scientist Lara Greaves told Manhire that some had floated encouraging supporters to split their vote – Te Pāti Māori for the electorate, Labour for the party vote – potentially generating several extra left-leaning MPs via overhang. But she warned the tactic carries real risk in the public’s view of the legitimacy of our electoral system.

post.text: If you wanted to undermine public confidence in MMP and give life to Luxo's wacky referendum notion, probably the easiest way would be to do what Te Pati Māori is proposing here and exploit the overhang to try to game MMP for cynical partisan advantage  thespinoff.co.nz/the-bulletin...
